cars.name: Benz Patent-Motorwagen

cars.story: The car begins as a purpose-built machine rather than a carriage conversion. Three wheels, an exposed engine and tiller steering make its unfamiliar layout visible at a glance.
cars.evidence: Top Gear treats the Patent-Motorwagen as the starting point for the production automobile.

cars.name: Model T
cars.title: The industrial revolution gets wheels.
cars.story: Affordability and repeatable manufacture turn the car into an everyday product. Its high, practical body belongs to an age when roads and ownership were both still being invented.

photos.description: Citroen DS21 Cabriolet at Knebworth Classic Car ShowAccording to the UK government database for taxing cars, this car was manufactured in 1962 but first registered in the UK in 2003. The steering wheel is on the left which confirms that when first registered it was almost certainly first registered outside the UK (maybe in Benelux or even France). BUT the arrangement of the front lights is consistent with the cars produced by Citroen in 1966/67. So ... even though the data on the UK government's tax data base are not always correct (and sometimes ridiculously wrong), the most likely scenario is that the car was indeed manufactured in 1962 and the front lights were changed in or after 1966.

photos.description: 1972 Lamborghini Miura P400 SV in Verde Chiaro with a powerful Blue interior in the parking lot of the 2025 Greenwich Concours d'Elegance. Chassis 5064 was originally painted white when it was sold to a pilot in White Plains, NY; it was the last Miura delivered new to the US. Factory air conditioning. This car was owned by Lamborghini test driver Bob Wallace in 1980, who restored it and upgraded it with numerous Jota spec items including a "seam-welded and reinforced chassis, uprated brakes and suspension, a deeper sump with baffles, lightened reduction gears with hard-chromed pins, independent transfer gear oilers, teflon-sealed oil intake guides, a full-flow oil radiator (in place of the A/C condenser, which was relocated), and breakerless electronic ignition."[1]

cars.name: Cybertruck
cars.title: The wedge returns as a pickup.
cars.story: Flat stainless-steel panels and a triangular roofline challenge the visual rules of the pickup. Its place here records a radical design experiment, without assuming commercial success or lasting influence.
cars.evidence: Top Gear explicitly discusses the rejection of conventional pickup design. Long-term industry influence is not awarded.
